title: The product of a multiset sum is the product of the parts
statement: For any two multisets over the naturals, the product of their sum is the product of their products. The two sides fold over three different bounds -- the sum's bound is the sum of the two bounds -- so neither factor's fold is a subfold of the left-hand side, and the proof collapses each tail rather than splitting a range.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Multiset.prod_add : ((x0 : AxNat.Multiset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Multiset) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Multiset.prod (AxNat.Multiset.add x0 x1)) (AxNat.mul (AxNat.Multiset.prod x0) (AxNat.Multiset.prod x1))))

evidence.supports: Nat.Multiset.prod_add is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Multiset.prod_add 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE '^Nat\.Multiset\.prod_add.2.\(\(x0 : AxNat\.Multiset\) -> \(\(x1 : AxNat\.Multiset\) -> Eq\.\{1\} AxNat \(AxNat\.Multiset\.prod \(AxNat\.Multiset\.add x0 x1\)\) \(AxNat\.mul \(AxNat\.Multiset\.prod x0\) \(AxNat\.Multiset\.prod x1\)\)\)\)$')" = 1

notes: This is the blocker `docs/plan/status/nat-multiset.md` handed off. Two candidates it named do not transport: `Int.prodRange_split` splits ONE function's fold at a point and leaves a SHIFTED fold behind, where what is needed is the upper half collapsing to 1; and `Nat.prodRangeIf` is a selector whose only theorems are `_zero`, `_succ` and `_congr_lt`. It says nothing about `Nat.Multiset.card` of a sum, and nothing about equality of the two multisets themselves -- `Nat.Multiset` has no extensional equality (ADR-1520), which is exactly why the uniqueness theorem is stated at the level of counts.
